set.plain: Does drinking young lead to alcohol problems later? This is not known. In the few studies that followed young people over time, in the US and Norway, drinking early went with more drinking problems as an adult in some studies, but in others the link went away once other risks, such as behaviour problems in adolescence, were taken into account. Feeling drunk at the first drink and starting to drink regularly went with later problems more strongly than the age of the first drink. In US twins, the twin who had drunk without their parents' permission by about age 15 drank more as an adult than the twin who had not, even in identical twins, though the difference was smaller than when all the young people in the study were compared; in identical twins, early drinking was not clearly linked to later symptoms of an alcohol disorder. Twin studies cannot rule out other differences between twins, such as smoking or other drug use. See the contested question.

evidence_set: Only five reports met the criteria: three from two US cohorts and two from two Norwegian cohorts (four cohorts in all), with samples of 447 to 1,311, all school- or community-based; three of them (2011 to 2013) published within the 3 years before the review.

set.plain: How often do people who use cocaine also use alcohol or cannabis? Often, in the studies one review found. On average, about 3 in 4 had used alcohol on the same occasion as cocaine or in the same period, and about 4 in 10 had used cannabis on the same occasion, 6 in 10 in the same period. But the numbers varied hugely between groups, from about a quarter to nearly everyone for alcohol and from about 1 in 10 to more than 9 in 10 for cannabis, depending on who was asked and exactly what was asked. This matters for research: none of 40 recent brain-scan studies of cocaine left out people who drink or use cannabis (two left out people who had used cannabis in the past week), so their results may mix up the effects of different drugs, while animal studies almost never gave a second drug. Tobacco was not counted.
